decisions.decision: A5: GET /v1/payments/:reference is the payer's own (user:owner); staff read GET /v1/admin/payments/:reference; nothing about a payment is public.
A6: An audit row's actor is a staff id (name joined on read); every staff action writes one, in the same transaction as the change.
A7: The server decides which actions a wish, person, payment or order offers (the response carries actions); it masks phone and email for staff (the full value only with a reason, audited).
A8: Staff sign-in: a code to an email that is already a staff member in Team; no self sign-up; staff refresh life 12 h (as declared). The code and verify routes are the only public /v1/admin routes.
A9: A maker sees only the Concierge orders given to them; owner and ops see all. Ops may read Prices; only owner and finance change them.

A10: A price change carries typed old and new values in kobo and takes effect as a new price-book version; the 40% and its end date live in the price book's Promotion, never a page constant. The payout threshold is a price-book setting (R14).

A11: A refund goes through the payments port and reads 'Refund started' until the provider's webhook confirms it; the ledger's provider side comes from a daily settlement job; differences are rows staff can see, never auto-corrected.

A12: Numbers' targets are a staff-set setting (none set: 'No target set'); thread counts are their own read (GET /v1/admin/support/counts); a reply really sends an email; an inbound email (the email provider's inbound webhook, signature checked: POST /v1/webhooks/email/inbound) opens or reopens a thread.

A13: Style use counts (previews, paid uses) are written by events from the app, never invented; a wish records the style it was made in (Wish.style). Automatic checks on a submitted style run in the page and are re-run by the reviewer's page; the server stores the result with who ran it.

A14: Every /v1/admin request that changes something carries reason (string, 4 or more characters), written to the audit row, including the declared ones that lacked it. Only the staff sign-in routes (code, verify, sign-out) take none; code and verify are public by nature (before sign-in), rate-limited.

decisions.decision: GG3: POST /v1/wishes/:id/pass-upgrade (signed in, the wish is the caller's own) turns a draft into a Signature wish by drawing one of the Pass's four upgrades. No money moves. It answers the wish (Wish). A draft with no ticket, a Moment or a Keepsake ticket may take it; a wish that is already a Signature or better, a wish that is not a draft, and an account with no live Pass or no upgrade left are refused (409 or 422). The draw is one conditional statement, so 20 at once with 1 left give one yes. A paid upgrade is not sold: the app and the documents give it no price (listed to the owner).

GG5: E-231 POST /v1/wishes/:id/seal body gains `usePass` (boolean, optional). usePass: true draws one wish from the Pass in the seal transaction, in place of a ticket payment (a wish with no ticket becomes a Keepsake; one that took a Pass upgrade stays a Signature); a wish that already holds a paid ticket is refused (422), an account with no live Pass wish left is refused (402). 20 at once with 1 left: one seals.

QQ2: DELETE /v1/admin/bans/:id (owner and ops) lifts a ban: sign-in works again; the listings it removed stay removed. It carries `reason` (DEC-125), writes one audit row and answers the Ban with `until` set to now. A ban not in force is 409.
VV1: E-231 POST /v1/wishes/:id/seal answers PaymentStartedOrCovered as E-228 does: {payment: null, item} when no money moves (the Pass or the plan pays), {payment, item} otherwise.

ZB3: E-231 body gains `usePlan` (boolean, optional). usePlan: true draws one wish from the business's Pro plan month or pack, in the seal transaction, in place of a ticket payment; the wish becomes a Signature with no ticket sold, writes its client-wish record and carries the business. It cannot be sent with usePass or over a wish that already holds a paid ticket (422).

decisions.topic: wish: hasPasscode in, legacy fields out
decisions.decision: VV3: the Wish contract gains `hasPasscode` (boolean: the wish has a passcode or an answer to ask; the passcode itself is never returned) and loses the legacy whole-wish fields the old app wrote (adds, blessing, call, captions, chapter, credits, details, effect, finale, letter, links, memory, note, off, on, photos, reasons, studio, timeline, type, voices and the like). A wish's words are in `content`.

decisions.topic: creator earnings: summary, accrual shape, bank
decisions.decision: WW7: RoyaltyAccrual loses `rows` and `total`. E-154 GET /v1/creator/earnings answers RoyaltyEarnings {items, nextCursor, summary}: the creator's accruals and reversals, newest first, and a summary {thisMonthKobo, waitingKobo, sendingKobo, paidKobo, byStyle[{styleSlug, amountKobo}]}. E-41 GET /v1/admin/creators: each Creator gains `bank` ({bankCode, accountNumber} with the number masked, or null). E-115's :id is the month (YYYY-MM).

decisions.topic: studio bodies, snapshot, style checks job
decisions.decision: XX4: E-186 PATCH /v1/studio/prefs body is the named keys, each optional: coached (boolean), bottom, span, addTab (strings), looks, recent, fav (arrays); a bad one is 422. E-192 POST /v1/studio/styles/:id/withdraw body is `on` (boolean, optional: the setTemplate form). SubmissionView gains `snapshot`: the frozen draft the checks and the reviewer read (T-63), or null. Job.type gains `check-style-submission`, the job that runs a submission's checks.

decisions.topic: contact page, saved replies, thread detail, delivery news
decisions.decision: YY3: POST /v1/support-threads/contact (public) opens a thread from the contact page: body {email, subject, body}; answers ThreadDetail; counted per network and per address, 5 a day each. The saved replies have a list and a writer: GET, POST, PATCH /:id and DELETE /:id on /v1/admin/support/saved-replies (ops, owner, support); a change carries `reason` (DEC-125) and writes one audit row; a SavedReply is {id, name, text}. ThreadDetail is a type: SupportThread with its `messages` (E-207, E-208, E-209 and the contact route answer it). MessageDelivery.status gains `bounced` and `complained`.

decisions.topic: reveal link off, the client's link, play shape
decisions.decision: EA2: POST /v1/business/reveal-links/:id/off (business) switches a link off at once and answers the RevealLink. The client's link: GET /v1/r/:code (public, no sign-in; x-unlock-token and x-reveal-session headers) answers RevealPlay: {state: 'passcode'} while a passcode is needed, otherwise {state: 'open', content, date, index, no, photos, style, business}; POST /v1/r/:code/unlock (public) takes {passcode} and answers UnlockResult. RevealPlay gains `state` and `business`; its other fields are absent in the passcode state.

decisions.topic: concierge: delivery, card, customer routes, states

closes.key: possible-alias|ConciergeOrder|ConciergeOrder fields due / dueAt may be one field
closes.detail: ConciergeOrder fields due / dueAt may be one field

decisions.decision: CA2: E-34 POST /v1/admin/concierge-orders/:id/delivery takes `wishIds` (array of wish ids, 1 to 1000: the wishes made for the order) beside `reason`. E-141 POST /v1/qr-cards takes `wishId` or `wishIds` (up to 100) and `names` (up to 100, each up to 200 characters), each optional; one of the two ids is needed. The customer's Concierge routes: GET /v1/concierge-orders (their own, a page), GET /v1/concierge-orders/:id, POST /v1/concierge-orders/:id/cancel (no body: the customer's own cancel); the staff cancel is POST /v1/admin/concierge/orders/:id/cancel (ops and owner; `reason`). E-36 answers a page of ConciergeOrder. E-148 POST /v1/wishes/:id/video answers PaymentStartedOrCovered. ConciergeOrder.status and .state gain `given` (a maker has the order) beside `making` (being made); ConciergeOrder gains paidAt, dueAt, paymentId and wishIds (the wishes delivered under it). ConciergeOrder.due (the list of due dates of a list order) and dueAt (the time a single wish is due) are two fields.

The registry is re-frozen after PP2, QQ1, QQ2, VV1, VV3, ZB3, WW7, XX4, YY3, EA2 and CA2 (DEC-189..199) by tools/pipeline/freeze.py; reconcile.py was run twice with --reopen (identical outputs, EXIT 0, 0 open conflicts, both admin gate lines 0). Endpoint ids already issued are unchanged; new ids follow. The other shared rulings of this base (OO4, PP1, PP3, QQ6, WW3, WW4, XX4 storage, YY1, YY2, ZZ5, ZB1, CB3, CB4, EA1) change storage, kernel or code, not the wire.
